questions.q: Drift speed of electrons, when $1.5A$ current flows in a copper wire of cross section $5{mm}^{2}$ is ${v}_{d} .$ If the electron density in copper is $9 \times {10}^{28}m^{- 3}$ the value of ${v}_{d}$ in $mms^{- 1}$ is close to (Take charge of an electron to be $= 1.6 \times {10}^{- 19}C$)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given,

Current,& $i = 1 . 5A$,

Cross-section of the wire,~$A = 5 \times {10}^{- 6}m^{2}$~and

Electron density,~$n = 9 \times {10}^{28}m^{- 3}$.

As current,~$i = neA{v}_{d}$

$⇒ 1.5 = 9 \times {10}^{28} \times 1.6 \times {10}^{- 19} \times 5 \times {10}^{- 6} \times {v}_{d}$

$⇒ {v}_{d} = 0.02mms^{- 1}$.

$C . S . = \dfrac{θ}{Ig}$

questions.q: Figure shows a part of an electric circuit. The potentials at points $a, b$~and $c$ are $30V, 12V$ and $2V$ respectively. The current through the~$20Ω$& resistor will be,
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Let the potential be& $xV$~at the junction.

By using~$V = IR$~we get,

$30 - x = 10{i}_{1}x - 12 = 20{i}_{2}x - 2 = 30{i}_{3}$

By using Kirchhoff's law,

${i}_{1} = {i}_{2} + {i}_{3}$

$⇒ \dfrac{30 - x}{10} + \dfrac{12 - x}{20} + \dfrac{2 - x}{30} = 0 ⇒ \dfrac{90 - 3x + 18 - 1 . 5x + 2 - x}{30} = 0$

$⇒ x = 20V$

The current through the~$20Ω$~resistor is~

${i}_{2} = \left(\dfrac{30 - 12}{20}\right)A$

$⇒ {i}_{2} = \dfrac{8}{20}A = 0 . 4A$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Resistance of bulb

$P = \dfrac{V2}{r}$

$r = \dfrac{( 100{)}^{2}}{500} = \dfrac{100 \times 100}{500} = 20$

$i = \dfrac{P}{V} = \dfrac{500}{100} = 5A$

$\Delta V$ in resistance $R = 100V$

$R = \dfrac{100}{5} = 20Ω$

questions.q: A wire of resistance ${R}_{1}R_{1}$ is drawn out so that its length is increased by twice of its original length. The ratio of new resistance to original resistance is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
As per the given question, the change in the length is& $∆ l = 2l$.

Resistance of a wire is given by,~$R = \dfrac{ρl}{A}$

Therefore,~${R}_{1} = ρ\dfrac{l1}{{A}_{1}}$

When the length is starched by~$2{l}_{1}$, final length will be~${l}_{2} = {l}_{1} + 2{l}_{1} = 3{l}_{1}$. As the volume remains constant~${l}_{2}{A}_{2} = {l}_{1}{A}_{1} ⇒ {A}_{2} = \dfrac{A1}{3}$. Therefore,

${R}_{2} = ρ\left(\dfrac{3{l}_{1}}{\dfrac{{A}_{1}}{3}}\right) = 9ρ\dfrac{l1}{{A}_{1}}$

$∴ \dfrac{R2}{R1} = 9$

questions.q: A current of $5A$ passes through a copper conductor (resistivity $= 1.7 \times {10}^{- 8}Ωm$ ) of radius of cross-section $5$ mm . Find the mobility of the charges if their drift velocity is $1.1 \times {10}^{- 3}\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm{ms}^{-1}$ .
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Mobility $\mu = \dfrac{{V}_{d}}{E}$
$⇒ \mu = \dfrac{Vd}{E} = \dfrac{{V}_{d}l}{V} = \dfrac{{V}_{d}l}{iR} = \dfrac{{V}_{d}Al}{iρl}$
$\mu = \dfrac{1.1 \times {10}^{- 3} \times \pi{\left(5 \times {10}^{- 3}\right)}^{2}}{5 \times 1.7 \times {10}^{- 8}}$
$= 1.0m^{2}V^{- 1}s^{- 1}$
